notes: Eclipse Loop 2.5.2 The mixer strip, finished: a fader you can read at a glance, a channel it rides in, no dead space — and playback that stays clean with the mixer open. The strip No dead band. The racks now grow into whatever height the strip has spare — inserts first, then sends — instead of leaving an empty gap under I/O. It is adaptive: a short window collapses back to showing the slots you have filled plus one empty, which is what you want when space is tight. A fader worth dragging. The throw is sized so there is resolution where you mix, around unity, without the fader becoming the tallest thing in the window. The meter now takes its height from the fader rather than carrying its own, so the two can never disagree about where the top is. A cap and a slot. The fader cap is tall rather than wide — the size a cap needs is in the direction it travels — dark, with lips top and bottom and a waist between them, and one crisp indicator line in the theme accent. The slot it rides in is a proper channel now: wider, with a shadowed wall and a lit lip, so the cap sits in something instead of being clipped to a hairline
